clue.text: Play hard to get about some drug

indicators.note: about means one word goes around another here, the coy word wrapping the drug

parts.note: someone playing hard to get is being coy
med is short for medicine, a drug of some sort

explanation.surface: Someone acts aloof while concerning themselves with a quantity of narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedy is a kind of stage play meant to amuse.

clue.text: People of intelligence without fun make a bloomer

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the agency goes around the fun

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
a lark is a bit of fun

explanation.surface: Clever folk who lack humour commit a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside'; 'bloomer' is not a gaffe but a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarkia is a genus of annual garden flowers, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Converter's way with Frenchman?

parts.note: a mode is a way or method
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a French gentleman

explanation.surface: A missionary's approach goes alongside a man from France.
explanation.definitionFit: A modem converts digital signals to analogue and back for transmission over a phone line.

clue.text: Dead skilful about a French college

indicators.note: about means the skilful word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: deft means skilful
un is French for a

explanation.surface: Someone clever has died concerning a French academy.
explanation.definitionFit: Defunct means no longer living or existing.

clue.text: Erotic will become sordid when time has elapsed

indicators.note: will become links the erotic word to the sordid one it turns into
has elapsed says the time letter goes away, so it is the piece standing inside

parts.note: seamy means sordid or squalid

explanation.surface: A racy story turns sleazy as the years pass.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards from the answer: take T (time) out of the erotic word and what remains is SEAMY, sordid. So the wordplay builds SEAMY with T placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy is a common informal word for sexually charged or erotic.

clue.text: In sleepy state, take hot slice

indicators.note: take means the sleepy word receives the hot letter inside it

parts.note: a trance is a dreamy, half-conscious state
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: While drowsy, someone grabs a warm portion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranche is a portion or slice, especially of money.

clue.text: Love for other — other paid

indicators.note: other means changed into a different form, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Affection for someone else, the other one paid.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'other' signals the rearrangement; the second is part of the fodder with 'paid'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek goddess of love, so the name can stand for love itself.

clue.text: Detectives give weapons to stick on the mast

parts.note: the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's police detectives
to arm is to supply with weapons

explanation.surface: Police officers hand out guns to be fixed to a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardarm is a spar fixed across a ship's mast, a stick on it.

clue.text: National leader (11) raised money for youth hostel

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the pieces are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: rent is money paid for lodging
YH is the abbreviation for youth hostel, as on maps

explanation.surface: The head of a nation collected funds for a backpackers' lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: The National is the National Theatre in London; 11 refers to the first name in the linked entries.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas Hytner was director of the National Theatre in London from 2003 to 2015.

clue.text: Taffy's home — right, left and roundabout

annotationWithheld.why: Taffy's home — right, left and roundabout (4,2,2,7): 'Taffy's home' defines the Welsh anthem title, but no parse found for 'right, left and roundabout' giving the letters
annotationWithheld.clue: Taffy's home — right, left and roundabout

clue.text: A key man, not unknown in ancient street

indicators.note: not says a letter is to be dropped from the phrase before it

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown, like x and z

explanation.surface: An important person, not identified, walks along an old road.
explanation.walkthrough: Akeman Street is a Roman road in southern England, running through Oxfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Akeman Street is the name of an old Roman road, so it is an ancient street.

clue.text: Dime reportedly divided in two, as put in by novel schoolteacher

indicators.note: put in tells us one piece is placed inside the other
reportedly means we go by what the words sound like when spoken

parts.note: a dime is ten cents, which 'divided in two' makes a pair of nickels, five-cent coins
taken as written

explanation.surface: A coin is split while a teacher from a book gets involved.
explanation.walkthrough: A US dime is worth ten cents, so 'divided in two' it is two five-cent nickels. The Dickens hero teaches at Dotheboys Hall, a Yorkshire school.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dickens hero of the novel of the same name works as an assistant master at a Yorkshire school.

clue.text: Rodent catcher who can't stop talking?

definitions.meaning: a person who hunts and traps rabbits for a living
in British slang to rabbit on is to chatter endlessly, so one who does is a chatterer

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a trapper of conies and, from the slang verb rabbit, a nonstop talker.

clue.text: Plant servant in county (Guardian article)

indicators.note: in places the servant inside the county abbreviation

parts.note: Beds is the short form of Bedfordshire, an English county
a lackey is a servant or footman
the Guardian newspaper, speaking of itself, says we or us
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A domestic worker employed in the shires is mentioned in a newspaper item.
explanation.walkthrough: Beds is Bedfordshire, a county north of London. 'Guardian' is the paper referring to itself, giving US.
explanation.definitionFit: Black-eyed Susan is the common name of a yellow daisy-like flower, Rudbeckia.

clue.text: Machine with gamma for chi when deciphered

definitions.text: Machine with gamma for chi when deciphered

indicators.note: deciphered suggests letters being unscrambled into a fresh order
for means one letter group stands in place of another in the word

parts.note: the Greek letter chi is written CH in English spelling
the Greek letter gamma corresponds to our G

explanation.surface: A coding device swaps one Greek letter for another during decryption.
explanation.walkthrough: In MACHINE replace CH (chi) with G (gamma) to get MAGINE, then rearrange as 'when deciphered' asks. The whole clue also describes the German wartime cipher machine.
explanation.definitionFit: The wartime German cipher device was called by this name, and the clue as a whole describes it.

clue.text: Zero tax on company with backing sheets

indicators.note: backing means the whole run of pieces is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A business avoids tax, with financial support, on its paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavo is a book size made by folding printing sheets into eight leaves, so it names such pages.

clue.text: Well in Essex (North) and on a roll

parts.note: Chigwell is an Essex town, so the part sitting in front of well there is chig

explanation.surface: A healthy person in an English county is on a list.
explanation.walkthrough: Chigwell is a town in Essex, near London: the clue reads 'well' in its name as the word and keeps the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A chignon is a knot or roll of hair worn at the back of the head.

clue.text: It's hard to bear when emperor follows round the States

indicators.note: follows means the emperor comes after the round letter

parts.note: O is round in shape
Nero was a Roman emperor
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A ruler trailing a lap of America finds it a burden.
explanation.definitionFit: Onerous describes a burden that is heavy to carry, so the clue's phrase is a fair paraphrase.

clue.text: Game for milkmaid on monument

definitions.meaning: a card game for one player, also called solitaire
the dairymaid heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera bearing her name
from Twelfth Night, 'sat like ___ on a monument, smiling at grief'

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a solitaire card game, the dairymaid of the operetta, and Shakespeare's figure on a monument.

clue.text: Spy out revolutionary loved by 6's child

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: An agent is unmasked as a radical adored by the son of a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is the goddess of love; her son is Eros, or Cupid, who loved Psyche in myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth Psyche was the mortal woman loved by Cupid, the son of the goddess at 6.

clue.text: Piece of advice on genealogy in Essex

parts.note: a tip is a helpful hint
a family tree records genealogy

explanation.surface: A suggestion about family history in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiptree is a village in Essex, a county east of London, famous for its jam maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiptree is a village located in the county of Essex, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Strong point of (roughly) detail (roughly)

parts.note: c, for circa, means roughly or approximately

indicators.note: roughly here means the letters are roughed up, put into a disorderly order

explanation.surface: An approximate description of the particulars, give or take.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'roughly' gives C (circa); the second rearranges DETAIL as ITADEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortress, a strongly defended point.

clue.text: See 11
Money placed in shot?

indicators.note: in tells us the placed word sits inside the shot word

parts.note: a pea is the ammunition fired from a peashooter
set means placed or put down

explanation.surface: Cash is put into a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was the currency of Spain before the euro.

clue.text: See 13
Setter's maternal relations are legally placed, keeping poor Tommy with the ladies

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the other pieces go within

parts.note: in football a player legally positioned is onside

indicators.note: poor suggests the name is in a bad way and comes out jumbled

parts.note: hers is what belongs to a woman, as on a ladies' sign

explanation.surface: A setter's female relatives are lawfully settled, housing a hard-up soldier among the women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter's' is the compiler speaking of 'my'. Tommy is slang for a British private soldier, which disguises the fodder; 'poor' turns TOMMY into MYMOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Relations through one's mother are said to be on that side of the family, and the setter says 'my'.

clue.text: One exposed as lunatic around the underworld

indicators.note: around means the lunatic word is wrapped about the other

parts.note: a nut is a crazy person
Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and a name for that realm

explanation.surface: Someone displayed as mad roams about hell.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes without clothes, so is exposed.

clue.text: Essential part of officer's report?

indicators.note: report means the sound of a word when spoken

parts.note: a colonel is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: The vital section of a military man's dispatch.
explanation.definitionFit: A kernel is the core or most important part of something.
